preop.why: A deep, smooth extubation without coughing, and no positive-pressure mask ventilation afterwards, protect the repair from pressure spikes and air entry (pneumocephalus).

steps.do: Expose the defect. Intrathecal fluorescein, where used, is off-label and must be dilute — commonly 0.1 mL of 10% fluorescein diluted in 10 mL of the patient's CSF or preservative-free saline, injected slowly over about 10 minutes; blue-light excitation viewed through a blue-blocking filter shows small or low-flow leaks.
steps.think: Is this the only defect? Where exactly are its bony margins?

steps.do: Remove mucosa from a rim around the defect; reduce any herniated tissue with bipolar to the skull-base level.
steps.think: Grafts adhere only to denuded bone.

steps.do: Place a graft (underlay between dura and bone where feasible) and an overlay free mucosal graft or vascularized flap; support with sealant and absorbable packing.
steps.think: Defect size and flow decide the layers: small low-flow defects close with a free graft; large or high-flow defects need multilayer plus vascularized cover. In one cribriform algorithm, a defect over about 5 mm (or any encephalocele) gets a free mucosal or pedicled septal graft rather than sealant and packing alone, and a rigid underlay of bone or cartilage (e.g. a composite graft from a split resected MT) is kept for encephaloceles; a cribriform leak without encephalocele closes without rigid material. A free mucosal graft goes mucosa-side toward the nose.

steps.do: Postoperative care: head elevation, no straining or nose blowing; non-absorbable packing, if used, stays at least 5 days, then saline sprays 4–6 times a day; lumbar drain only selectively (when used, about 10–15 mL/h for 2–5 days, then clamped and observed before removal); treat raised intracranial pressure.
steps.think: Does this patient need intracranial pressure management to protect the repair long-term?

endpoints: No leak on Valsalva at the end of surgery
Graft in contact with denuded bone all around
pitfalls: Missed second defect
Graft on mucosa rather than bone
Ignoring intracranial hypertension
Free mucosal graft laid with its mucosal surface against the bone — a mucocele can form

procedures.name: Endoscopic anterior skull-base encephalocele repair
indications: Meningoencephalocele through the cribriform plate, lateral lamella or ethmoid roof (congenital, spontaneous or traumatic)
procedures.corridor: Olfactory cleft or ethmoid, depending on the defect site.

preop.check: MRI to confirm brain/meninges in the sac and exclude a tumor
preop.why: A mass in the olfactory cleft must never be biopsied before imaging.

preop.check: Intracranial pressure risk factors
preop.why: Spontaneous encephaloceles often reflect intracranial hypertension.

steps.do: Expose the sac and the surrounding skull base.
steps.think: Is the stalk's bony defect fully in view?

steps.do: Reduce the herniated tissue with bipolar cautery down to the skull base; never avulse it.
steps.think: Vessels in the stalk can retract intracranially — cut, don't pull.

steps.do: Denude the bone margins and repair in layers as for a CSF leak.
steps.think: Is the repair sized for the defect, not for the sac? ([[p.csf-leak-repair]]) When brain has herniated, a rigid underlay (bone or cartilage) is often added to resist the raised intracranial pressure.

endpoints: Herniated tissue reduced to skull-base level
Defect closed in layers
pitfalls: Traction on the sac
Untreated intracranial hypertension

stations.name: Bulla and middle meatus, 0°
stations.where: Right: scope tip at the MT head in the middle meatus, MT gently medialized, looking posterolaterally at the bulla behind the resected uncinate.
stations.purpose: Orient the anterior ethmoidectomy: identify the bulla, the hiatus and the retrobullar recess before opening the bulla low and medially.

stations.name: Basal lamella, 0°
stations.where: Right: scope tip in the opened bulla cavity, looking straight back at the wall behind the retrobullar recess, lamina papyracea on the right of the screen.
stations.purpose: Pick the inferomedial entry point into the posterior ethmoid and confirm the lamina laterally.

stations.name: Posterior ethmoid skull base, 0°
stations.where: Right: scope tip through the basal lamella in the posterior ethmoid, angled slightly up and back toward the sphenoid face.
stations.purpose: Identify the skull base where it is broadest, see the PEA, and check for an Onodi cell before going forward along the roof.

stations.name: Ethmoid roof and AEA, 30°
stations.where: Right: scope tip in the mid-ethmoid below the roof, 30° lens turned up and forward, following the skull base from posterior to anterior.
stations.purpose: Clear the roof from behind forward and find the AEA before the frontal recess.

stations.name: Olfactory cleft, 0°
stations.where: Right: scope passed between the septum and the MT head, advanced up and back into the cleft.
stations.purpose: Assess the cleft for polyps or a mass and see the medial side of the skull base without dissection.

stations.name: Frontal recess entry above the axilla, 45°
stations.where: Right: scope tip at the MT axilla in the middle meatus, 45° lens looking up toward the agger nasi and frontal recess.
stations.purpose: Relate the agger nasi cell, upper uncinate and bulla to the recess; plan which wall to remove first.

stations.name: Frontal recess to ostium, 70°
stations.where: Right: scope tip in the middle meatus below the frontal recess, 70° lens pointing straight up the recess toward the ostium.
stations.purpose: Identify the drainage pathway between the cells and remove the cell caps without touching the pathway's mucosa.

stations.name: Inside the frontal sinus, 70°
stations.where: Right: scope tip at the enlarged frontal ostium, 70° lens looking up into the sinus.
stations.purpose: Check the sinus for residual cell walls, disease and the posterior table before finishing.

stations.name: Draf III common cavity, 0°
stations.where: Scope in one nostril, tip below the septal window just behind the nasal beak, looking up at both frontal sinus floors.
stations.purpose: Keep the drill anterior to the frontal T and first olfactory fibres while taking the beak and floors forward and laterally.

stations.name: Medial orbital floor through the antrostomy, 30°
stations.where: Right: scope tip at a wide middle meatal antrostomy, 30° lens turned up and lateral to the antral roof.
stations.purpose: Fix the height of the medial orbital floor as the reference for posterior ethmoid and sphenoid entry (Casiano).

stations.name: Medial orbital wall after full ethmoidectomy, 0°
stations.where: Right: scope tip in the completed sphenoethmoidectomy cavity, looking laterally at the lamina from the frontal recess back to the sphenoid face.
stations.purpose: Orbital decompression and subperiosteal abscess drainage: define the wall to remove, the strut and the skull-base margin.

stations.name: Frontal recess, parasagittal overview
stations.where: Overview: parasagittal cut through the frontal recess, viewed from medial.
stations.purpose: Teach the hourglass and the building-block reading of the recess cells and pathway.

stations.name: Olfactory fossa, coronal overview
stations.where: Overview: coronal cut through the anterior ethmoid at the level of the AEA, viewed from in front.
stations.purpose: Show Keros depth and Gera angle and why the medial roof is the weak point.

stations.name: Anterior cranial fossa from above
stations.where: Overview: looking down on the anterior cranial fossa floor with the frontal lobes removed.
stations.purpose: Relate the transcribriform resection field to the intracranial anatomy.

pathways.name: Frontal sinus drainage (lamina insertion of the uncinate)
pathways.note: Usual pattern: the uncinate inserts on the lamina papyracea or agger nasi, closing a terminal recess, so the frontal sinus drains medial to the uncinate directly into the middle meatus. Within the recess the path runs around the cells: medial/posterior to anterior cells, anterior to posterior cells, lateral to a frontal septal cell ([[c.ifac]]).

pathways.name: Frontal sinus drainage into the infundibulum
pathways.note: When the uncinate inserts on the skull base or the MT ([[c.uncinate-superior-attachment]]), the frontal sinus drains lateral to the uncinate into the ethmoid infundibulum; the upper uncinate must then be removed to open the recess.

pathways.name: Frontal sinus mucociliary clearance
pathways.note: Mucus travels up the medial wall (intersinus septum), across the roof, down the anterior and posterior walls and laterally, then medially along the floor to the ostium; part of it recirculates back up the medial side, which is why a separate trephination or drill hole away from the natural path does not drain the sinus.

pathways.name: Anterior ethmoid mucociliary route
pathways.note: Anterior ethmoid secretions join the frontal and maxillary flow in the middle meatus and pass to the nasopharynx anterior and inferior to the eustachian tube orifice.

pathways.name: Posterior ethmoid mucociliary route
pathways.note: Posterior ethmoid and sphenoid secretions pass through the sphenoethmoidal recess and reach the nasopharynx posterior and superior to the eustachian tube orifice.
